props.title: 50 Children

sections.content: **50 Children: The Rescue Mission of Mr. and Mrs. Kraus** (2013) stands among the most powerful yet overlooked Holocaust rescue documentaries. This HBO film chronicles Gilbert and Eleanor Kraus, who undertook an extraordinary mission in 1939 to save Jewish children from Nazi Germany. The film shares DNA with other crucial Holocaust documentaries like **The Last Days** (1998) and **Into the Arms of Strangers: Stories of the Kindertransport** (2000), but offers a uniquely American perspective on civilian heroism.

sections.content: The film's power lies in its methodical documentation through archival footage, photographs, and interviews with surviving children. Like **Paper Clips** (2004), it demonstrates how individual action can create profound change. The Krauses' mission to save 50 children required navigating both Nazi bureaucracy and American immigration restrictions, highlighting themes that resonate with **Who Will Write Our History** (2018) about the Warsaw Ghetto archivists.

What sets **50 Children** (2013) apart is its focus on American civilian response to the Holocaust before US entry into WWII. While films like **The Good Nazi** (2018) and **Weapons of the Spirit** (1989) explore European rescuers, this documentary illuminates early American awareness and response to the growing crisis, making it essential viewing alongside **America and the Holocaust** (2022). SUBHEAD: Civilian Heroism During the Holocaust

The film connects to a broader category of documentaries about civilian rescuers like **The Rescuers** (2011) and **Nicky's Family** (2011) about Nicholas Winton's rescue of 669 children. These works collectively challenge the narrative of widespread passive acceptance of Nazi persecution, showing how ordinary people took extraordinary risks to save lives.
